[Agent]: Hi, thank you for calling customer care. How can I help you today?
[Caller]: This is my third time contacting you about the internet inside our office building. The service quality has been poor, and the performance has been awful.
[Agent]: I’m sorry this has continued. What symptoms are you seeing, and which devices are affected?
[Caller]: Our video meetings lag constantly, and the download throughput is only around three to five megabits per second. Several laptops and tablets cannot stay connected. We also keep seeing a “Connection failed” message.
[Agent]: Have you restarted the gateway since the problem began?
[Caller]: Yes, I reset it twice this morning. It did not help. I cannot do my job reliably with the service behaving like this.
[Agent]: I can see instability on the connection. I’m going to refresh the connection profile and reprovision the gateway now.
[Caller]: A technician already visited last Tuesday, but the same issue came back. How much longer is this going to take to resolve?
[Agent]: I’ve completed the reprovisioning and sent a new configuration to the gateway. Please test the connection again.
[Caller]: It connected, but given the repeated problems and the time I’ve lost, I would like a service credit.
[Agent]: That is reasonable. I have applied a $35 credit to the account, and it will appear on your next statement.
[Caller]: Thank you. I hope the connection remains stable this time.
[Agent]: You’re welcome. I’ve also documented the prior contacts and technician visit in case additional troubleshooting is required.
